root_cause: When the wstETH market held almost nothing, the excess of flash-loan repayments was added to `lending_accumulator`, driving it very high, and withdrawals burned shares as amount divided by the accumulator rounded down, so too few shares were burned and repeated deposits and withdrawals took out more than was put in.
audit_scope: zkLend v1 market contract and its zToken contracts as deployed on Starknet mainnet (market 0x04c0a5193d58f74fbace4b74dcf65481e734ed1714121bdc571da345540efa05)
notes: Market address from the zkLend contracts documentation and the Verichains analysis. Transactions from BlockSec (initial deposit, flash-loan manipulation, first raw_balance manipulation, one attack cycle), copied as printed; the last one omits a leading zero. 0x04d7191dc8eac499bac710dd368706e3ce76c9945da52535de770d06ce7d3b26 is the attack contract (BlockSec) and is not listed as a contract. No public v1 source: the zkLend GitHub organization only has zklend-v2-core and claim-calculator (checked 2026-09-25), and whether the class is source-verified on Voyager or Starkscan could not be checked (HTTP 403). The official post-mortem also returned 403; the root cause follows BlockSec and Verichains. The protocol wound down after the incident, so there is no fix commit. Symbols are the function and variable names used by BlockSec.

root_cause: The CAPO price cap depends on the pair `snapshotRatio` and `snapshotTimestamp`, but the on-chain update path only limited how fast the ratio may grow (3% per 3 days) and did not constrain or re-derive the timestamp, so when the off-chain risk oracle updated both, the ratio was clamped while the timestamp moved to a 7-day-old anchor, the pair no longer matched, and the computed cap fell below the market rate.
audit_scope: src/contracts in aave-dao/aave-risk-agents together with the CAPO adapter source verified on Etherscan (src/contracts/PriceCapAdapterBase.sol and src/contracts/lst-adapters/WstETHPriceCapAdapter.sol)
notes: Contracts: WstETHPriceCapAdapter (verified, emitted CapParametersUpdated with snapshotRatio 1191926196478762900 and snapshotTimestamp 1772535647); a TransparentUpgradeableProxy that emitted UpdateInjected, whose implementation 0x73d1BDCdb39eF06Aea0371288a3cA5f1559Ffcba is verified as AgentHub; and the risk oracle that received publishBulkRiskParameterUpdates. Transactions (from rekt.news): parameter update 2026-03-10 11:45:59 UTC, execution via Chainlink Automation 11:46:11 UTC, and the later borrow-cap reduction. The post-mortem does not name the contract that enforces the ratio limit. aave-dao/aave-risk-agents main has AaveCapoAgent validating ranges only for snapshotRatio and maxYearlyRatioGrowthPercent; whether the agent deployed on 2026-03-10 matches that code was not confirmed, so no vulnerable commit is pinned. Part of the cause is the closed off-chain Edge risk oracle logic, and the remediation (consistent timestamp derivation, pre-submission bound checks) was off-chain, so there is no fix commit. The adapter source also lives in bgd-labs/aave-capo (now aave-dao/aave-price-feeds).

root_cause: The Realms governance configuration set the community pass threshold at about 1% of total supply while participation was very low, used a zero-second transaction hold-up time and had no veto, so one address holding bought tokens could pass a proposal alone and its hidden treasury-transfer instruction executed right after passing.
audit_scope: Governance configuration of realm 84pGFuy1Y27ApK67ApethaPvexeDWA66zNV8gm38TVeQ (its governance accounts and treasury) and how the SPL Governance program applies it to proposal voting and execution
notes: Configuration-level issue, not a program bug: SPL Governance executed as configured. Accounts are the realm (from the Realms proposal URL), the BonkDAO treasury and the BIP #76 proposal; the transaction is the treasury drain; all from rekt.news. Attacker-side wallets, not listed as contracts: proposal creator 8xxRdtzsw1CJWfEahViqNjZwh5dYJAdSbBctWwcbycVo, main voter CyEE7oHVDaFJ5xZLbXY3h2Z2uk1VwhTkdy72kPUEtypQ, second voter FQnQYaYe1UiQZiokdDH39ybRbhJYfzzwXSghnA32pWxc, drain receivers 9bxWkNf3BtJ6iehq9KbX9uCWMjem4TFiPZ19T2sYJHvQ and EXaJnmrLf7RAKLfn1hehoKX94keKYmvZm5H5zuYVeh42. Configuration values (1% threshold, zero-second hold-up, 100 million BONK to create a proposal) are from Rekt and Halborn and were not read from chain. Symbol names are GovernanceConfig fields in SPL Governance (solana-labs/solana-program-library, governance/program/src/state/governance.rs); the governance program ID and version this realm uses were not confirmed, so no verified source is given. Result recorded as hit; the quorum-cost half was partial.

classes: Assumptions broken by callbacks and reentrancy
root_cause: The core IBC message server handlers `Timeout` and `TimeoutOnClose` called the application's `OnTimeoutPacket` callback before `TimeoutExecuted` deleted the packet commitment, so a callback that re-entered (through ibc-hooks into a CosmWasm contract) and submitted the same timeout again still found the commitment and passed replay protection; the fix deletes the commitment before the callback.
notes: Call order read directly in modules/core/keeper/msg_server.go at v8.1.1 (callback, then TimeoutExecuted) and v8.2.0 (TimeoutExecuted, then callback). 5e2e9ebc is 'Merge pull request from GHSA-j496-crgh-34mx' on the v8 line; GitHub's diff for it also lists unrelated release-line files, and only the msg_server.go change (10 additions, 10 deletions) is the fix. Also fixed in 4.6.0, 5.4.0, 6.3.0 and 7.4.0; those commits were not looked up. Reaching the bug needs an app stack where ibc-hooks wraps ICS-20 and can call CosmWasm contracts (the ibc-hooks middleware lives outside ibc-go, in the Osmosis repository). No CVE; reported through the Cosmos HackerOne program; no exploitation reported.

component: Upgradeable EVM spoke contracts (Arbitrum, Optimism, Ethereum)
root_cause: An upgrade of the spoke contracts that added pause and unpause state shifted the storage layout, so the `initialized` flag was read from a slot that held zero; `initialize()` could be called again to take the privileged role, after which `upgradeToAndCall()` could switch the proxy to any implementation.
audit_scope: Pike spoke implementations before and after the pause upgrade on Ethereum (0x634683d7079af2EBeC84637BBC29dbD6FE817564 and 0xD167A1893e8F108572826dAbAe19663A9131b0c2) behind proxy 0xFC7599cfFea9De127a9f9C748CCb451a34d2F063, compared for storage layout and initialization guards; bytecode only
notes: Contracts are on Ethereum: the proxy (emitted Initialized and Upgraded in the Ethereum exploit transaction), the implementation before the pause upgrade and the implementation after it (the latter two named by CertiK; all three share creator 0xb1eA97c9F68978905fB1Bf5089E71A073bC4f5C8 on Etherscan). Transactions are the 2024-04-30 exploit on Ethereum, Arbitrum and Optimism, from CertiK; the Arbitrum and Optimism proxy addresses were not recorded. In the Ethereum transaction the proxy was upgraded to 0x1da4Bc596BFb1087f2F7999b0340Fcba03C47fbD (attacker-supplied), sent from 0x19066f7431df29A0910d287C8822936Bb7D89E23 (Etherscan label Pike Finance Exploiter). None of the three contracts is source-verified on Etherscan (checked 2026-09-25); the public nutsfinance/pike-protocol repository is an early beta with 3 commits and was not confirmed to match the deployed spokes. The first exploit (2024-04-26) is a separate incident and is not covered here. Root cause from CertiK; no fix commit is public.

classes: Whether declared controls actually take effect
root_cause: `update_v2` in `typus_oracle::oracle` computed `vector::contains(&update_authority.authority, &tx_context::sender(ctx))` but did not `assert!` the result, so the authority check was discarded and any sender could set oracle prices; the fix rewrote authorization around an `UpdateCap` that is asserted against the sender.
notes: Vulnerable update_v2 read directly at dfa236ab07ac6456febb0ab5f07baa8328d91817 (parent of the fix). The fix commit is titled 'Update oracle' and is a larger refactor (UpdateCap and UpdateCaps, new pyth_parser interface, 5 files); its oracle.move hunk was not read, and the asserted UpdateCap line is quoted from the mehvetero analysis. That analysis also names a commit a918e98 (2025-09-24) as the vulnerable version; it does not resolve in Typus-Lab/typus. Package ID and the first attack transaction digest are from the mehvetero post on the Sui forum and were not checked on an explorer; whether the published package bytes match the repository was not checked. The module (deployed 2024-11-13) was outside the May 2025 MoveBit audit scope; the drained pool logic is in typus_perp/sources/tlp/lp_pool.move.

classes: Multiple representations of the same fact
root_cause: `validate_ed25519_signature_instruction` checked the Ed25519 program ID, data length, signature count and empty accounts, but read the signer public key and message hash at fixed offsets 16 and 112 instead of parsing the offsets and instruction indexes inside that instruction's data, so the bytes the Ed25519 program verified could differ from the bytes the depository compared; the fix parses `public_key_offset` and `message_data_offset` and reads through them.
notes: Vulnerable function read directly at 4b615f62127d3ebdd808e7f8c29b0cc2ab4db55b (parent of the fix). The fix commit is 'feat: various tweaks for relay-depository (#28)'; it replaces the fixed slices with offsets parsed from the instruction header; whether it also validates the signature and instruction-index fields was not read. The program ID is the declare_id! at the vulnerable ref and is labeled Relay Bridge on Solana Compass; the on-chain program was not checked against this source. Repository archived 2026-09-09 and merged into a settlement-protocol repository. Privately disclosed by Asymmetric Research and patched; no exploitation reported, so there are no incident transactions.

root_cause: `executeWithoutChainIdValidation` deliberately lets one signature replay `removeOwnerAtIndex` on every chain, but that function identified the owner only by index, and the same index can hold different owners on different chains, so a replay could remove the wrong owner, with no guard against removing the last owner; the fix makes the caller pass the owner bytes and checks them against the index, and a follow-up blocks removing the last owner through that function.
notes: PR #42 (merge commit e77e62e4dac687f92f4d51eaf815b12aadb770d2, 2024-04-02) adds the owner check; PR #43 (merge commit 9c1cf9ea91abbf1c2a6da6420a04d2cca67a3f13, 2024-04-03) adds the last-owner guard and removeLastOwner. canSkipChainIdValidation allowing removeOwnerAtIndex was read directly in src/CoinbaseSmartWallet.sol at e77e62e4. The contest snapshot is code-423n4/2024-03-coinbase at e0573369b865d47fed778de00a7b6df65ab1744e, where the file is src/SmartWallet/MultiOwnable.sol; either repository works for a blind audit. Audit-contest finding; no on-chain incident.

id: Solana ZK ElGamal proof program "phantom challenge" (2025-06)
root_cause: In `PercentageWithCapProof`, a sigma OR proof, the prover-chosen branch challenge `c_max_proof` was not appended to the Fiat-Shamir transcript before the verifier derived its random challenge, so a prover could choose it after seeing that challenge and forge fee proofs; the fix appends `c_max_proof` to the transcript.
notes: e285e47 (PR #6523, 2025-06-12) adds the one transcript line in percentage_with_cap.rs plus feature gates to disable and re-enable the ZK ElGamal proof program; it was reverted on master the same day by fd8bc3ae936351f18deeaa47d5ae6fa5cb182263 (PR #6544). The v2.2 branch never received the transcript line; mitigation was disabling confidential transfers in Token-2022 and then disabling the proof program by feature activation (epoch 805). zk-sdk was later removed from agave (PR #7126, 2025-07-30) and now lives in solana-program/zk-elgamal-proof; the fix there was not identified. Native runtime program, not a deployed contract; reported 2025-06-10, no exploitation reported. The file history also has an earlier commit 7751625 'ZK Fix - hash the scalar proof components into the transcript' (2025-04-18) from a different, earlier bug in the same program (see https://solana.com/tr/news/post-mortem-may-2-2025).

root_cause: When accepting deposit messages from TON, the bridge sequencer checked neither that the sender Jetton wallet's code hash was the standard wallet code nor that the wallet's recorded minter was the expected Jetton master, so well-formed bridge messages from a counterfeit wallet were taken as real deposits and unbacked assets were minted on TAC.
notes: Closed-source off-chain sequencer: question-level test only. The listed contract is the attacker-deployed counterfeit Jetton wallet and the transaction is its bridge message to the TAC proxy, both from the official post-mortem, which gives no TAC bridge contract addresses. Attacker addresses: TON EQBPHhXyG_vbsAEnB6YccNhhaVc6I3ixOCc7vriaOzo4AFA8, TAC EVM 0xB8D5E0a0100361fb0c67085Fc122F64de2D796BD. Fixes listed in the post-mortem: code-hash check against the canonical Jetton wallet code, check of the wallet's Jetton master, rejection of unverifiable senders, per-minter rate limits and circuit breakers. The TON documentation later made the code-hash check a baseline (ton-org/docs commit 2a8c11d7588402d5173435b4730e8b7079b51314).

component: Langflow low-code AI workflow platform (CISA KEV)
root_cause: The `/api/v1/validate/code` endpoint required no login, and its validation passed function definitions from the submitted code to `exec`, where decorators and default arguments run at definition time; the fix adds the `CurrentActiveUser` dependency to the endpoint.
notes: PR #6911 'fix: auth current user on code validation' merged 2025-03-05 as faac4db1; it changes only the endpoint signature plus tests, so validate_code still reaches exec for logged-in users. Released in 1.3.0. validate_code is imported from langflow.utils.validate (path inferred from the import; the exec call there was not read). GHSA-c995-4fw3-j39m is a withdrawn duplicate. The record's root-cause source is the Horizon3 analysis 'Unsafe at Any Speed'; in CISA KEV (added 2025-05-05 per the record).

component: Ray dashboard and jobs API (CISA KEV)
root_cause: The dashboard decided whether a request came from a browser only by checking whether `User-Agent` starts with `Mozilla`, which fetch in Firefox and Safari can change, so with DNS rebinding a web page could POST jobs to the local jobs API; the fix also rejects requests that carry `Sec-Fetch-*` headers.
notes: Fix commit 'Add denial of fetch headers (#58553)' adds has_sec_fetch_headers() and uses it in browsers_no_post_put_middleware and the deny_browser_requests decorator; the record's wording 'added origin checks' is looser than the patch. Fixed in 2.52.0 (affected below 2.52.0). The jobs API runs the submitted entrypoint as a shell command by design, so the browser check was the only barrier for unauthenticated local dashboards. In CISA KEV (2026-08-17 per the record).

component: LiteLLM LLM gateway, MCP streamable HTTP endpoint (CISA KEV)
root_cause: In the MCP streamable HTTP auth handler, when LiteLLM key validation failed with 401 or 403 and an `Authorization` header was present, the OAuth2 passthrough fallback returned an empty `UserAPIKeyAuth()` and carried on, so any Bearer token could open a session and list and call MCP tools; the fix allows the fallback only when every targeted MCP server is configured for OAuth2.
notes: PR #26463 'fix(mcp): tighten public-route detection and OAuth2 fallback gating' merged 2026-04-30 and shipped in 1.84.0; the GitLab advisory cites commit 73869f0f, while the PR page shows merge commit 2e561bd04e9964861a83acb9226bfecc701162c6. The fix adds _target_servers_use_oauth2 to gate the fallback. The same PR also fixed public-route detection that matched '.well-known' anywhere in the URL, including the query string. The record says 1.84.0 removed the fallback; the patch gates it instead. In CISA KEV (2026-09-02 per the record).

root_cause: The Proxy authentication interceptor skipped all authentication when the `sourceId` request header, base64-decoded, equaled the internal constant `@@milvus-member@@` hard-coded in the source for component-to-component calls; the fix removes the sourceId check and the member credential entirely.
audit_scope: internal/proxy (authentication and gRPC interceptors) and internal/util/grpcclient
notes: Refs are for the 2.6 line: PR #45379 'enhance: [2.6] skip check source id' merged 2025-11-07 into hotfix-2.6.4 as e938bacf, released in 2.6.5. PR #45383 fixes 2.5 (2.5.21) and PR #45391 fixes 2.4 (2.4.24). Files and removed symbols read from the PR diff. The Cyborg analysis cited in the record was not rechecked.

root_cause: When loading a `.keras` archive, `_retrieve_class_or_fn` imported and returned any module and function named in `config.json`, and `safe_mode=True` only blocked the lambda route; the fix restricts that module lookup and checks that each deserialized layer is a Keras `Operation`.
notes: PR #20751 'Added checks to serialization.' merged 2025-01-12 as e67ac8ff (2 files, 18 additions, 16 deletions); released in 3.9.0, affected 3.0.0 to 3.8.x. The Tower of Hanoi report cited in the record was not rechecked.

classes: Multiple representations of the same fact
root_cause: `dumps()` and `dumpd()` did not escape plain dicts that carry the reserved `lc` key, and `load()` and `loads()` rebuilt framework objects from such dicts when reading back, with `secrets_from_env=True` by default so secret references were filled from environment variables; the fix escapes user dicts, defaults `secrets_from_env` to `False` and adds an `allowed_objects` allowlist.
notes: 5ec0fa69 is PR #34455 on master (langchain-core 1.2.5); d9ec4c5c is its backport PR #34458 on v0.3 (0.3.81). The fix adds libs/core/langchain_core/load/_validation.py (escaping with __lc_escaped__) and an init_validator that blocks Jinja2 templates by default. File list read from the commits; the old defaults are as stated in the advisory.

component: Codex CLI local coding agent sandbox
root_cause: The sandbox policy used the command's `cwd`, which the model can set, as the writable root, so a model-chosen directory outside the session folder became writable; the fix passes a separate sandbox-policy cwd taken from where the user started the session.
notes: The GHSA names no commit. 8595237 'fix: ensure cwd for conversation and sandbox are separate concerns' (PR #3874, 12 files) is linked to the CVE by third-party databases (Miggo, SentinelOne) and matches the advisory text; the vendor link was not confirmed. Fixed in @openai/codex 0.39.0 and the IDE extension 0.4.12; affected @openai/codex 0.2.0 to 0.38.0. Network restriction of the sandbox was not affected.

root_cause: The Content Security Policy allowlist for Agentforce output still held an expired domain (`my-salesforce-cms.com`) that anyone could register, so instructions submitted through a public Web-to-Lead form could make the agent embed CRM data in an image URL on that domain; Salesforce enforced Trusted URLs and reclaimed the domain.
notes: Closed SaaS: question-level test only. No CVE. Reported 2025-07-28; Trusted URLs enforcement for Agentforce and Einstein AI shipped 2025-09-08; public disclosure 2025-09-25. Root cause from the Noma Labs report and Salesforce's statement as quoted in press coverage.

root_cause: The admission controller for tenant pods rejected only running as root and allowed every other UID (and `shareProcessNamespace`), so a tenant pod could run as the Istio sidecar's UID 1337, whose traffic Istio's iptables rules exempt, defeating network isolation; internal services behind that isolation (Grafana Loki, EFS, Tiller) did not authenticate.
notes: Closed vendor platform: question-level test only. No CVE. Root cause from the Wiz report; SAP fixed all reported issues by 2024-05-15 per the record. Result partial: the UID exemption half only got a direction, the unauthenticated internal services half was a hit.

component: Amazon Q Developer VS Code extension build and release pipeline
root_cause: A GitHub token in the extension's AWS CodeBuild configuration was scoped more broadly than the build needed, so an outside party could use it to commit a malicious prompt to the repository, which the automated release shipped in 1.84.0; the credentials were revoked and replaced and 1.85.0 removed the code.
notes: The flaw is in AWS-side CodeBuild project configuration (token scope), which is not in the public repository, so this is a question-level test only; the repository (which has buildspec/ and .github/) is listed for context. Affected: extension 1.84.0 only (withdrawn); fixed: 1.85.0. The malicious code failed to run because of a syntax error. The facet mapping is loose: the rows hit were specialties 4.33 'Token permissions' and dimensions 36 'Build and release permissions'. A related bulletin is AWS-2025-016.
